# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## 1. BY PRIMARY MECHANIC

### 1.1 Loop/Path Drawing
*The solver must draw a continuous loop or path through the grid.*

#### 1.1.1 Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** — Loop constrained by black/white circle turn rules
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn on grid edges, constrained by number clues
- **Mid-loop** — Loop where black circles are midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** — Directed loop with wind constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop alternating between moon/sun rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop with straight-or-turn constraints per region
- **Suraromu** — Loop passing through numbered gates in order

#### 1.1.2 Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** — Loop that avoids black cells; arrow clues indicate black cell counts

#### 1.1.3 Path Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect number pairs with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect islands with bridges (1 or 2) to form a connected network

---

### 1.2 Cell Shading / Painting
*The solver must color certain cells black (or leave them white).*

#### 1.2.1 Shading with Connectivity Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form one connected wall; white islands match given numbers; no 2×2 black
- **Nurimisaki** — Black/white shading with promontory (dead-end) constraints; no 2×2 of either color
- **Kurotto** — Shading around numbered circles (sum of adjacent black groups)
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers count visible white cells; black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected
- **Heyawake** — Shading in rooms; white cells can't span 3+ rooms in a line; no adjacent black cells
- **Norinori** — Exactly two black cells per region, each forming a domino
- **Nuritwin** — Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected; no 2×2
- **LITS** — Place one tetromino per region; no same-shape adjacency; connected; no 2×2

#### 1.2.2 Shading with Geometric Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Black groups must be rectangles; white groups must not be rectangles
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles to match row/column clue counts (pictorial output)

#### 1.2.3 Shading with Dropping/Gravity
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms; when "dropped," they fill bottom half of grid

#### 1.2.4 Shading with Deception
- **Usowan** — Like Akari/Heyawake shading but one clue per room is a liar

#### 1.2.5 Elimination Shading
- **Hitori** — Black out duplicate numbers so none repeat in rows/columns; no adjacent black; white connected

---

### 1.3 Region Division / Partitioning
*The solver must divide the grid into regions/blocks.*

#### 1.3.1 Rectangular Partitioning
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area

#### 1.3.2 Polyomino Partitioning
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding block edges
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks where white and gray halves are congruent

#### 1.3.3 Number-Based Partitioning
- **Fillomino** — Fill numbers and partition into polyominoes of matching size; same-size blocks can't touch

---

### 1.4 Number/Symbol Placement
*The solver must fill cells with numbers or symbols.*

#### 1.4.1 Latin-Square Family
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes without repetition

#### 1.4.2 Room-Based Number Fill
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1 to N; arrows indicate largest neighbor; no same-number adjacency across rooms
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with 1 to N; duplicate numbers in a line must be spaced apart ≥ the number's value

#### 1.4.3 Crossword-Style Number Fill
- **Nansuke** — Place numbers from a given list into a crossword-like grid

#### 1.4.4 Directional Symbol Fill
- **Juosan** — Fill cells with horizontal (—) or vertical (|) bars; territory clues; limited consecutive runs

---

### 1.5 Object Placement
*The solver must place specific objects (light bulbs, blocks, shapes) into cells.*

#### 1.5.1 Light/Illumination
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs to illuminate all white cells; numbers constrain adjacent bulb count; no bulb-to-bulb visibility

#### 1.5.2 Shape/Block Placement
- **Chained Block** — Place black-cell blocks with specific sizes; blocks chain at corners; unique shapes per chain
- **Evolomino** — Place growing polyomino blocks along arrow paths
- **Pencils** — Mark out pencil shapes and draw lines from their tips

#### 1.5.3 Snake Placement
- **Hebi** — Place numbered snakes (1–5) with visibility and territorial constraints

---

### 1.6 Movement / Transformation
*The solver must move given objects to satisfy constraints.*

- **Satogaeri** — Move circles within countries so each country has exactly one; numbered circles move exact distances; paths don't cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move circles into gray areas via straight arrows; sums must match; arrows don't cross

---

### 1.7 Maze Construction
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint rooms to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path; triangles not on shortest path

---

## 2. BY CONSTRAINT TYPE (Cross-cutting)

### 2.1 Numeric Clues
| Constraint Style | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Adjacency count** | Akari, Shakashaka, Five Cells, Usowan |
| **Visible/reachable cell count** | Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Akari |
| **Sum of adjacent groups** | Kurotto |
| **Area/block size** | Shikaku, Fillomino, Chained Block, Choco Banana, Nuritwin, Double Choco, Sashigane |
| **Room fill (1 to N)** | Makaro, Ripple Effect |
| **Separation distance** | Ripple Effect |
| **Gate/sequence ordering** | Suraromu |
| **Movement distance** | Satogaeri |
| **Target sums** | Yosenabe |
| **Surrounding line count** | Slitherlink |
| **Directional count** | Yajilin, Hebi |

### 2.2 Connectivity Constraints
| Constraint | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **White cells connected** | Hitori, Heyawake, Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Usowan |
| **Black cells connected** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **Single loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Yajilin, Suraromu |
| **Connected network (bridges)** | Hashiwokakero |
| **No 2×2 black** | Nurikabe, LITS, Sto-stone, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin |
| **No 2×2 white** | Nurimisaki |
| **No adjacent black** | Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Yajilin, Usowan |

### 2.3 Shape Constraints
| Constraint | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Rectangles only** | Shikaku, Choco Banana (black groups), Shakashaka (white regions) |
| **Non-rectangles required** | Choco Banana (white groups) |
| **L-shapes only** | Sashigane |
| **Tetrominoes** | LITS |
| **Pentominoes** | Five Cells |
| **Congruent pairs** | Double Choco, Nuritwin |
| **Progressive growth** | Evolomino |
| **Unique shapes per chain** | Chained Block |

---

## 3. BY GRID ELEMENT USED

### 3.1 Edge-Based
- **Slitherlink** (lines on edges between dots)
- **Hashiwokakero** (bridges between nodes)

### 3.2 Cell-Center Based
- **All loop puzzles** (lines through cell centers)
- **All shading puzzles** (cells colored)
- **All number placement puzzles** (numbers in cells)

### 3.3 Region/Room Based (Bold-line Boundaries)
- Heyawake, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Double Choco, Norinori, Five Cells, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, LITS, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Nuritwin, Suraromu, Juosan

### 3.4 Arrow/Directional Clues
- Yajilin, Hebi, Makaro, Nagareru, Sashigane, Evolomino, Yosenabe

### 3.5 Circle Clues (Black/White)
- Masyu, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop, Kurotto, Satogaeri, Nurimisaki, Sashigane, Hashiwokakero

---

## 4. BY OUTPUT TYPE

### 4.1 A Pattern of Shaded Cells
Akari, Chained Block, Choco Banana, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Norinori, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Nurimeizu

### 4.2 A Closed Loop
Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Yajilin, Suraromu

### 4.3 Paths/Connections
Numberlink, Hashiwokakero

### 4.4 A Partitioned Grid
Shikaku, Five Cells, Fillomino, Sashigane, Double Choco

### 4.5 A Completed Number Grid
Sudoku, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Nansuke, Fillomino

### 4.6 Symbol/Mark Grid
Juosan, Hebi, Evolomino, Pencils

### 4.7 Moved Objects with Arrows
Satogaeri, Yosenabe
